# Issue tracking procedure (agent quick reference)

<!-- Generated by skill `init-dsh-project` v1.8 on 2026-10-26. -->

**The rules live in [`../issues/README.md`](../issues/README.md)** (the split from the ledger,
lifecycle, format, index table). This file only covers what to do with your hands.

## Opening one

```bash
# 1) take the next number (read the last index row, or list the directory)
ls docs/issues/ | sort | tail -3
# 2) copy the template
cp docs/issues/0000-template.md docs/issues/00N-<slug>.md
# 3) fill it in, then add a row to the index table in docs/issues/README.md in the **same commit**
# 4) run the gate
python3 tools/dev/check_docs.py --only index
```

## How status moves

| Event | Do |
|---|---|
| Starting | add `in-progress (<date>)` to `Status:` |
| Done | re-run the `## Exit` criteria → paste `## Evidence` → `closed-verified (<date>)` |
| Deferred | `⏸ DEFERRED (<date>) → <where the decision lives>`, with the rationale in an ADR |
| Closed | update the index row's status column; drop one line into the ledger via `kms project log` |

## Cross-references

- issue ↔ ADR: cross-link with relative paths (`../adr/0007-slug.md`).
- issue ↔ research: relative paths (`../research/<date>-<slug>.md`).
- **Cross-repo**: write coordinates (`<repo> issue NNN`), never a relative path — the gate cannot
  resolve a path outside the repo, so it becomes a permanent dead link.
- Carry the issue number in the commit message: `fix(<scope>): <what> (#NNN)`.

## Graduating from the ledger

Once a line in the ledger's "next steps" **needs repro steps and verifiable criteria**, it
graduates into an issue: create the file + the index row, write "from ledger next steps, <date>"
under `Context`; and **rewrite the ledger line into a one-line pointer**. Ordering belongs to the
ledger, detail belongs to the issue — **never keep two copies of the same prose**.

## A mechanical Exit criterion belongs in the gate, not in prose

An `## Exit` line like "no doc states a bare figure" or "every rejected option records why" is a
check somebody will run **once**, by hand, when the issue closes — and then never again. The next
doc written six weeks later breaks it silently, because nothing re-runs a sentence.

So when an Exit criterion is mechanical, **land it as a check**:

| Criterion shape | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Holds for every project in the family | a new check inside `tools/dev/check_docs.py` (upstream it — siblings need it too) |
| True of *this* repo only | a rule in `tools/dev/check_conventions.py` (the gate's one seam; see its header) |
| Genuinely needs judgement | stays prose, and says so — an unjudgeable Exit line is `needs-info` |

Then paste the check into `## Evidence` as the command that was re-run, not as a grep transcript.
Two disciplines make such a check worth having, and both are hard requirements:

1. **Measure the trigger's precision before shipping.** A check that mostly reports noise teaches
   its readers to ignore the *whole* gate — worse than having no check. Run the rule over the
   existing tree and count how many hits are real; narrow the trigger until it is close to 100%.
2. **Falsify it — do not just watch it go green.** Inject a violation, confirm the check turns red
   **and** the process exit code becomes non-zero, then remove the injection. A check that prints
   a failure and returns 0 will be trusted, and that is the expensive part.

Corollary: **an Exit criterion nobody can re-run is not an Exit criterion.** If the only way to
check it is to read carefully, say that out loud in the issue so the reader knows what they are
being asked to do.

## Relation to the vault

- Progress → `kms project log d2r-mobile -t "<title>" --body "<2-5 line digest>"` (the ledger is a
  dashboard, not a journal: short digest + link out).
- Counter-intuitive traps / tool knowledge → `30-Areas/Technology/<tool>.md`, not the ledger body.
